components.description: KV cache growth and the limits of eviction motivate ARM's routed fixed-size memory with learnable writes and adaptive reads, evaluated on benchmarks

nodes.name: KV cache growth limits long context
nodes.description: KV cache memory grows linearly with context length, rapidly surpassing the model's own memory footprint and degrading decoding latency, which hinders long-context inference.

nodes.name: Existing remedies have limitations
nodes.description: Quantization, pruning/eviction and offloading each retain a limitation: a still-growing cache, risk of discarding important information, or inter-hierarchy transfer latency.

nodes.name: Eviction treats importance as certain
nodes.description: Eviction-based policies implicitly use a one-hot write weight, discarding all but one write candidate and assuming certainty about future access; they cannot adapt to task-specific importance.

nodes.name: Hierarchical routed memory
nodes.description: ARM organizes the KV cache as a fixed multi-level tree of routers whose leaf buckets each hold a fixed number of KV slots; each token is deterministically routed root-to-leaf by the largest routing logit, with routers trained by a self-supervised objective.

nodes.name: Learnable soft writes
nodes.description: ARM selects bucket slots via Gumbel-Softmax and updates them with sigmoid-gated combinations of new and stored content, so new information is softly integrated without hard eviction and the cache size stays constant.

nodes.name: Adaptive Top-M retrieval
nodes.description: A policy trained as an MDP learns per-input and per-layer how many memory buckets (Top-M) to retrieve, enabling sparse access for simple inputs and expanded retrieval for harder ones.

nodes.name: Gated shared writes are optimal under uncertainty
nodes.description: Under i.i.d. Gaussian write candidates, optimal gated weights w*=pi make a shared slot retain information in proportion to anticipated usage, with I(a_r; A | r) >= -(d/2) log(1-||pi||_2^2), so sharing capacity beats one-hot eviction.

nodes.name: Experimental setup
nodes.description: ARM is built on Llama3-8B, pre-trained on a 10B-token FineWeb-Edu subset, with 256 memory slots (4-level tree, 4 children per node) compared against full attention, sliding window, StreamingLLM, KIVI quantization and CPU offloading.

nodes.name: No loss on non-generative tasks
nodes.description: On language modeling and zero-shot commonsense tasks (Table 1), adapting the pre-trained model to ARM causes minimal change in average performance and perplexity, as with standard caching.

nodes.name: ARM works on long-context benchmarks
nodes.description: ARM outperforms standard eviction baselines on LongBench (Table 3) and RULER up to 128K context (Table 4), e.g. TREC 62.5 vs 38.0 for full attention in Table 3.

nodes.name: Latency and memory benefits
nodes.description: ARM gives significant generation speedup over full-cache methods (full attention, quantization), is on par with sliding window and sink caches, and offloading has the same memory use but significant latency problems (Fig 2).

structural_reasoning: Problem and limits of prior cache management lead to the ARM design (routed memory, soft writes, adaptive reads), theory for gated writes, and empirical evaluation.
